vsm2.16:87.1:
87. 11. As to simile: The truth of suffering should be regarded as a burden, the truth of origin as the taking up of the burden, the
truth of cessation as the putting down of the burden, the truth of the path as the means to putting down the burden (see S III 26),
vsm2.16:87.2:
The truth of suffering is like a disease, the truth of origin is like the cause of the disease,
the truth of cessation is like the cure of the disease, and the truth of the path is like the medicine.
vsm2.16:87.3:
Or the truth of suffering is like a famine, the truth of origin is like a drought,
the truth of cessation is like plenty, and the truth of the path is like timely rain.
vsm2.16:87.4:
Furthermore, these truths can be understood in this way by applying these similes: enmity, the cause of the enmity,
the removal of the enmity, and the means to remove the enmity; a poison tree, the tree’s root, the cutting of the root,
and the means to cut the root; fear, the cause of fear, freedom from fear, and the means to attain it; the hither shore,
the great flood, the further shore, and the effort to reach it. This is how the exposition should be understood as to simile.
vsm2.16:88.1:
88. 12. As to tetrad: (a) there is suffering that is not noble truth, (b) there is noble truth that is not suffering,
(c) there is what is both suffering and noble truth, and (d) there is what is neither suffering nor noble truth.
vsm2.16:88.2: So also with origin and the rest.
vsm2.16:89.1:
89. Herein, (a) though states associated with the path and the fruits of asceticism are suffering
since they are suffering due to formations (see §35) because of the words, “What is impermanent
is painful” (S II 53; III 22), still they are not the noble truth of suffering,
vsm2.16:89.2: (b) Cessation is a noble truth but it is not suffering,
vsm2.16:89.3:
(c) The other two noble truths can be suffering because they are impermanent, but they are not so in the real
sense of that for the full-understanding of which (see §28) the life of purity is lived under the Blessed One.
vsm2.16:89.4: The five aggregates as objects of clinging, except craving, are in all aspects both suffering and noble truth.
vsm2.16:89.5:
(d) The states associated with the path and the fruits of asceticism are neither suffering in the real
sense of that for the full-understanding of which the life of purity is lived under the Blessed One, nor are they noble truth.
vsm2.16:89.6: Origin, etc., should also be construed in the corresponding way. This is how the exposition should be understood here as to tetrad.
vsm2.16:90.1:
90. 13. As to void, singlefold, and so on: firstly, as to void: in the ultimate sense all the truths should be understood
as void because of the absence of (i) any experiencer, (ii) any doer, (iii) anyone who is extinguished, and (iv) any goer.
vsm2.16:90.5:
So void of lastingness, and beauty, pleasure, self,
Is the first pair, and void of self the deathless state,
And void of lastingness, of pleasure and of self
Is the path too; for such is voidness in these four.
vsm2.16:91.1: 91. Or three are void of cessation, and cessation is void of the other three.
vsm2.16:91.2:
Or the cause is void of the result, because of the absence of suffering in the origin, and of cessation in the path;
the cause is not gravid with its fruit like the Primordial Essence of those who assert the existence of Primordial Essence.
vsm2.16:91.3:
And the result is void of the cause owing to the absence of inherence of the origin in suffering and of the path in cessation;
the fruit of a cause does not have its cause inherent in it, like the two atoms, etc., of those who assert inherence.
vsm2.16:91.6: This, in the first place, is how the exposition should be understood as to void.
vsm2.16:92.1: 92. 14. As to singlefold and so on: and here all suffering is of one kind as the state of occurrence.
vsm2.16:92.2: It is of two kinds as mentality-materiality.
vsm2.16:92.3: It is of three kinds as divided into rebirth-process becoming in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere.
vsm2.16:92.4: It is of four kinds classed according to the four nutriments.
vsm2.16:92.5: It is of five kinds classed according to the five aggregates as objects of clinging.
vsm2.16:93.1: 93. Also origin is of one kind as making occur.
vsm2.16:93.2: It is of two kinds as associated and not associated with false view.
vsm2.16:93.3: It is of three kinds as craving for sense desires, craving for becoming, and craving for non-becoming.
vsm2.16:93.4: It is of four kinds as abandonable by the four paths.
vsm2.16:93.5: It is of five kinds classed as delight in materiality, and so on.
vsm2.16:93.6: It is of six kinds classed as the six groups of craving.
vsm2.16:94.1: 94. Also cessation is of one kind being the unformed element.
vsm2.16:94.2: But indirectly it is of two kinds as “with result of past clinging left” and as “without result of past clinging left”;
vsm2.16:94.3: and of three kinds as the stilling of the three kinds of becoming;
vsm2.16:94.4: and of four kinds as approachable by the four paths;
vsm2.16:94.5: and of five kinds as the subsiding of the five kinds of delight;
vsm2.16:94.6: and of six kinds classed according to the destruction of the six groups of craving.
vsm2.16:95.1: 95. Also the path is of one kind as what should be developed.
vsm2.16:95.2: It is of two kinds classed according to serenity and insight, or classed according to seeing and developing.
vsm2.16:95.3: It is of three kinds classed according to the three aggregates;
vsm2.16:95.4: for the path, being selective, is included by the three aggregates, which are comprehensive, as a city is by a kingdom,
vsm2.16:95.6:
“The three aggregates are not included in the Noble Eightfold Path, friend Visākha, but the Noble Eightfold Path
is included by the three aggregates. Any right speech, any right action, any right livelihood: these are included in the virtue
aggregate. Any right effort, any right mindfulness, any right concentration: these are included in the concentration aggregate.
Any right view, any right thinking: these are included in the understanding aggregate” (M I 301).
vsm2.16:96.1:
96. For here the three beginning with right speech are virtue and so they
are included in the virtue aggregate, being of the same kind.
vsm2.16:96.2:
For although in the text the description is given in the locative case as “in the virtue aggregate,”
still the meaning should be understood according to the instrumental case that is, “by the virtue aggregate.”
vsm2.16:96.3:
As to the three beginning with right effort, concentration cannot of its own nature cause absorption
through unification on the object; but with energy accomplishing its function of exerting and mindfulness
accomplishing its function of preventing wobbling, it can do so.
vsm2.16:97.1:
97. Here is a simile: three friends, thinking, “We will celebrate the festival,” entered a park.
Then one saw a champak tree in full blossom, but he could not reach the flowers by raising his hand.
vsm2.16:97.2:
The second bent down for the first to climb on his back. But although standing on the other’s back,
he still could not pick them because of his unsteadiness.
vsm2.16:97.3: Then the third offered his shoulder as support.
vsm2.16:97.4:
So standing on the back of the one and supporting himself on the other’s shoulder, he picked as many
flowers as he wanted and after adorning himself, he went and enjoyed the festival.
vsm2.16:97.5: And so it is with this.
vsm2.16:98.1:
98. For the three states beginning with right effort, which are born together,
are like the three friends who enter the park together.
vsm2.16:98.2: The object is like the champak tree in full blossom.
vsm2.16:98.3:
Concentration, which cannot of its own nature bring about absorption by unification on the object,
is like the man who could not pick the flower by raising his arm.
vsm2.16:98.4: Effort is like the companion who bent down, giving his back to mount upon.
vsm2.16:98.5: Mindfulness is like the friend who stood by, giving his shoulder for support.
vsm2.16:98.6:
Just as standing on the back of the one and supporting himself on the other’s shoulder he could pick as many flowers as he wanted,
so too, when energy accomplishes its function of exerting and when mindfulness accomplishes its function of preventing
wobbling, with the help so obtained concentration can bring about absorption by unification on the object.
vsm2.16:98.7:
So here in the concentration aggregate it is only concentration that is included as of the same
kind. But effort and mindfulness are included because of their action in assisting.
vsm2.16:99.1:
99. Also as regards right view and right thinking, understanding cannot of its own
nature define an object as impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.16:99.2: But with applied thought giving assistance by repeatedly hitting the object it can.
vsm2.16:100.2:
Just as a money changer, having a coin placed in his hand and being desirous of looking at it on all sides equally,
cannot turn it over with the power of his eye only, but by turning it over with his fingers he is able to look at it on all
sides, similarly understanding cannot of its own nature define an object as impermanent and so on.
vsm2.16:100.3:
But assisted by applied thought with its characteristic of directing the mind on to the object and its function
of striking and threshing, as it were, hitting and turning over, it can take anything given and define it.
vsm2.16:100.4:
So here in the understanding aggregate it is only right view that is included as of the same
kind. But right thinking is included because of its action in assisting.
vsm2.16:101.1: 101. So the path is included by the three aggregates.
vsm2.16:101.2: Hence it was said that it is of three kinds classed according to the three aggregates.
vsm2.16:101.3: And it is of four kinds as the path of stream-entry and so on.
vsm2.16:102.1: 102. In addition, all the truths are of one kind because they are not unreal, or because they must be directly known.
vsm2.16:102.2: They are of two kinds as (i and ii) mundane and (iii and iv) supramundane, or (i, ii, and iv) formed and (iii) unformed.
vsm2.16:102.3:
They are of three kind as (ii) to be abandoned by seeing and development, (iii and iv)
not to be abandoned, and (i) neither to be abandoned nor not to be abandoned.
vsm2.16:102.4:
They are of four kinds classed according to what has to be fully understood, and so on (see §28).
This is how the exposition should be understood as to singlefold and so on.
vsm2.16:103.1:
103. 15. As to similar and dissimilar, all the truths are similar to each other because they
are not unreal, are void of self, and are difficult to penetrate,
vsm2.16:103.3:
“What do you think, Ānanda, which is more difficult to do, more difficult to perform, that a man should shoot
an arrow through a small keyhole from a distance time after time without missing or that he should penetrate
the tip of a hair split a hundred times with the tip of a similar hair?”— “This is more difficult to do, venerable sir,
more difficult to perform, that a man should penetrate the tip of a hair split a hundred times with the tip of a similar
hair.”—“They penetrate something more difficult to penetrate than that, Ānanda, who penetrate correctly thus,
‘This is suffering’ … who penetrate correctly thus, ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering’” (S V 454).
vsm2.16:103.4: They are dissimilar when defined according to their individual characteristics.
vsm2.16:104.1:
104. And the first two are similar since they are profound because hard to grasp,
since they are mundane, and since they are subject to cankers.
vsm2.16:104.2: They are dissimilar in being divided into fruit and cause, and being respectively to be fully understood and to be abandoned.
vsm2.16:104.3:
And the last two are similar since they are hard to grasp because profound,
since they are supramundane, and since they are free from cankers.
vsm2.16:104.4:
They are dissimilar in being divided into object and what has an object,
and in being respectively to be realized and to be developed.
vsm2.16:104.5: And the first and third are similar since they come under the heading of result.
vsm2.16:104.6: They are dissimilar in being formed and unformed.
vsm2.16:104.7: Also the second and fourth are similar since they come under the heading of cause.
vsm2.16:104.8: They are dissimilar in being respectively entirely unprofitable and entirely profitable.
vsm2.16:104.9: And the first and fourth are similar in being formed.
vsm2.16:104.10: They are dissimilar in being mundane and supramundane.
vsm2.16:104.11: Also the second and the third are similar since they are the state of neither-trainer-nor-non-trainer (see Vibh 114).
vsm2.16:104.12: They are dissimilar in being respectively with object and without object.
vsm2.16:104.13:
A man of vision can apply
By suchlike means his talent so
That he among the truths may know
The similar and contrary.
vsm2.16:104.14:
The sixteenth chapter called “The Description of the
Faculties and Truths” in the Treatise on the Development
of Understanding in the Path of Purification composed for
the purpose of gladdening good people.
